subject: paediatrics
title: Child health programmes and child protection

steps.tx: Child health in India is delivered through **IMNCI**, the Indian adaptation of IMCI, which covers newborns and children up to five years. It is the central pillar of child interventions under the RCH strategy. Its main highlights include early neonatal care, inclusion of the first seven days of life, and home based care of newborns and young infants. Training starts with the young infant, and half the training time is spent on infants aged 0 to 2 months.

steps.tx: Perinatal mortality covers deaths from 28 weeks of gestation to 7 days after birth. Neonatal mortality covers deaths in the first **28 days**. Post-neonatal mortality covers deaths from 28 days to one year, usually from causes such as SIDS, infections and trauma. Infant mortality covers the first year of life. Stillbirth is defined from 28 weeks of gestation.

steps.tx: Child abuse includes **battered baby syndrome**, where injuries appear at different stages of healing. Classic signs are bruises in various stages, spiral shaft fractures, metaphyseal corner (chip) fractures, posterior rib fractures and retinal haemorrhages. **Subdural haematoma** with retinal haemorrhage and diffuse axonal injury strongly suggests abusive head trauma, formerly called shaken baby syndrome. Nobbing fractures of the rib near the spine are also described.

steps.tx: Sudden infant death syndrome is the unexpected death of an infant under one year that remains unexplained after a full post-mortem. Peak age is 2 to 4 months. Risk factors include prone sleeping, maternal **smoking**, male sex, prematurity and soft bedding. Honey has been linked with **Clostridium botulinum** toxin as a suspected cause, so it should be avoided in infants.

steps.tx: Key programme facts: POSHAN Abhiyaan was launched in March 2018 and focuses on the first **1000 days** of life. Iron and folic acid for children aged 6 months to 5 years is 20 mg elemental iron with 100 microgram folic acid daily. Among Indian states, Goa has the lowest infant mortality rate in SRS 2017. Road traffic accidents are the commonest injury death in children.
